lesson.child_mission: Giving change is the difference between the amount paid and the price. Count on from the price to the tender, or subtract.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Find change: price $2.45, paid $5; price $6.10, paid $10.

FEEDBACK
$2.55; $3.90.

WATCH FOR
Subtracting dollars only and forgetting cents underpays or overpays change.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Solve ten change problems (prices under $20). Show count-on or subtraction working. For two items, list a possible set of coins/notes that make the change.

Write a short reflection naming one step you corrected and why.

materials: Optional: place-value chart or number line

Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Solve ten change problems (prices under $20). Show count-on or subtraction working. For two items, list a possible set of coins/notes that make the change. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 2: Sample misconception: Subtracting dollars only and forgetting cents underpays or overpays change.. Correction uses $2.55; $3.90.. Why: restores accurate change.

Parent: Likely misconception: Subtracting dollars only and forgetting cents underpays or overpays change. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Solve one fresh problem that uses change with different numbers from the worked model. Show working and name the places or values that matter.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Describe one likely mistake with change, show corrected working, and say why the correction works.

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
Item $3.20, pay with $5. Change: count on 80c to $4, then $1 to $5 → $1.80. Or $5.00−$3.20=$1.80.

TRY FIRST
Find change: price $2.45, paid $5; price $6.10, paid $10.

FEEDBACK
$2.55; $3.90.
teach_steps.explain:
Giving change is the difference between the amount paid and the price. Count on from the price to the tender, or subtract.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner choose methods based on place value, quantity and accurate working, rather than guessing digits by shape alone. Keep every step justified.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the places, values or distances that carry the method. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your working with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your reasoning? If a digit or place is uncertain, identify what would have to be regrouped or counted again. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
teach_steps.notice: Subtracting dollars only and forgetting cents underpays or overpays change. Correct the value or method, not just the appearance of the digits.
